arcos-animas-quimixto.name: Arcos – Ánimas – Quimixto
arcos-animas-quimixto.headline: Ánimas – Quimixto
arcos-animas-quimixto.short: Snorkeling at the pinnacles of Los Arcos, lunch at Las Ánimas and a stop in Quimixto. Departs 9:00 am from the Puerto Vallarta dock.
arcos-animas-quimixto.pitch: Snorkeling at the pinnacles of Los Arcos, lunch at Las Ánimas and a waterfall in Quimixto.
arcos-animas-quimixto.blurb: Eight hours that start with breakfast on board and end with salt on your skin. You swim among the pinnacles of Los Arcos, eat facing Las Ánimas and get off at Quimixto to walk to the waterfall. If it is your first time on the bay, this trip tells the whole story.
arcos-animas-quimixto.photoAlt: The pinnacles of Los Arcos seen from the sea

itinerary.title: Puerto Vallarta dock
itinerary.body: Check-in, life jacket and breakfast on board while the captain checks the sea report.

itinerary.title: We sail towards Los Arcos
itinerary.body: Half an hour hugging the south shore; the pinnacles appear in the distance.

itinerary.title: Snorkeling at Los Arcos
itinerary.body: An hour among the pinnacles and caves of the marine park, with the guide in the water.

itinerary.title: Lunch at Las Ánimas
itinerary.body: Grilled fish facing the beach and free time for kayaking or a hammock.

itinerary.title: Return from Quimixto
itinerary.body: A short walk to the waterfall and back to the dock with the sun low. Arrival around 5:30.

faq.question: Do I need to know how to swim?
faq.answer: No. The life jacket floats on its own and the guide stays with you in the water. Anyone who would rather not go in can watch Los Arcos from the deck.

faq.question: What if it rains?
faq.answer: With light rain we sail anyway; the bay is usually calm. If the harbormaster closes the port, you change the date or we refund the deposit.

faq.question: Can children come?
faq.answer: Yes, from 4 years old. We carry life jackets in every size and lunch at Las Ánimas gives them beach time.

faq.question: How much walking is there in Quimixto?
faq.answer: About 25 minutes along a trail to the waterfall. Anyone who would rather not walk stays on the beach or rides up on horseback at their own expense.

reviews.quote: The sea was calm and the snorkeling was incredible. We are coming back next month.
reviews.author: Paulina T.

reviews.quote: Eight hours and not a minute of waiting. Lunch at Las Ánimas, feet in the sand, was the best part.
reviews.author: Rodrigo and Ana

reviews.quote: The guide got in the water with the kids and taught them to use the snorkel. They came out beaming.
reviews.author: The Cortés family

yelapa-majahuitas.name: Yelapa – Majahuitas
yelapa-majahuitas.headline: Yelapa – Majahuitas
yelapa-majahuitas.short: A village with no road, a waterfall and the beach at Majahuitas. Snorkel gear, lunch and an open bar on board.
yelapa-majahuitas.pitch: A village with no road, a waterfall and the beach at Majahuitas, lunch and bar on board.
yelapa-majahuitas.blurb: Yelapa has no road: you arrive by sea and get around on foot. You climb to the waterfall, eat on the beach at Majahuitas and come back feeling you have been far away, even though you leave and return the same day.
yelapa-majahuitas.photoAlt: Boat off the beach at Yelapa

itinerary.title: Puerto Vallarta dock
itinerary.body: Check-in, life jacket and coffee. The captain explains the route and when we land on each beach.

itinerary.title: We sail south
itinerary.body: An hour along the coast; on the way you see Los Arcos and Las Ánimas from the boat.

itinerary.title: Yelapa and the waterfall
itinerary.body: A walk through the village up to the waterfall. A swim in the pool and a slice of banana pie on the way back.

itinerary.title: Lunch at Majahuitas
itinerary.body: A beach with no road and no signal. Lunch facing the sea and snorkeling from the shore.

itinerary.title: Return
itinerary.body: Back to the dock with the bar open. Arrival around 5:00.

faq.question: How far is the walk to the waterfall?
faq.answer: About 20 minutes through the village streets, with a gentle climb. Sandals work, but sneakers are better.

faq.question: Is there phone signal at Majahuitas?
faq.answer: No. It is part of the charm: let people know before you leave that you will be offline until five.

faq.question: Can I pay in cash?
faq.answer: The deposit is by bank transfer or card; the balance is paid at the dock in cash or by card.

faq.question: Can children come?
faq.answer: Yes, from 4 years old. The walk is easy and the beach at Majahuitas has no waves.

reviews.quote: Everything sorted: transport, food and snorkeling. We just showed up at the dock and it was all ready.
reviews.author: Daniel R.

reviews.quote: Majahuitas is another planet. We ate with our feet in the water and there was nobody else on the beach.
reviews.author: Lucía V.

reviews.quote: The waterfall was worth every step. So was the banana pie in Yelapa.
reviews.author: Marco and Teo

islas-marietas.name: Marietas Islands
islas-marietas.headline: Marietas Islands
islas-marietas.short: A biosphere reserve an hour from Nuevo Vallarta. Snorkeling at the Hidden Beach, bird watching and lunch on board. Groups of 12 at most.
islas-marietas.pitch: A biosphere reserve: the Hidden Beach, sea birds and groups of twelve people.
islas-marietas.blurb: Twelve people, one guide and an island the reserve protects. You swim into the Hidden Beach, see birds that nest nowhere else in Mexico and eat on board while the boat rocks. Worth booking weeks ahead.
islas-marietas.photoAlt: The Hidden Beach seen from the sea

itinerary.title: Nuevo Vallarta dock
itinerary.body: Check-in, life jacket and breakfast on board. The guide hands out the reserve wristbands.

itinerary.title: We sail
itinerary.body: An hour towards open sea. In season we often cross paths with whales on the way.

itinerary.title: Hidden Beach
itinerary.body: You swim in through the tunnel with the guide, in the slot the reserve assigns us.

itinerary.title: Snorkeling and birds
itinerary.body: Snorkeling at Isla Redonda and a slow lap of Isla Larga to see the blue-footed booby.

itinerary.title: Return
itinerary.body: Lunch on board on the way back to Nuevo Vallarta. Arrival around 2:00.

faq.question: Is entry to the Hidden Beach guaranteed?
faq.answer: The reserve issues a limited number of wristbands per day and we hold them with your booking. If the sea does not allow entry, that day is swapped for snorkeling at Isla Redonda and we refund the difference.

faq.question: Do I need to know how to swim?
faq.answer: For the Hidden Beach, yes: you swim about 30 meters through a tunnel. Non-swimmers enjoy the rest of the trip from the boat.

faq.question: Why groups of 12?
faq.answer: It is the most the reserve allows per boat. That is why it pays to book weeks ahead.

faq.question: Can children come?
faq.answer: Yes, from 6 years old and swimming well. Under-6s cannot enter the Hidden Beach under the reserve's rules.

reviews.quote: The captain took us to a cave where there was nobody else. The best day of the trip.
reviews.author: Alexandra G.

reviews.quote: We left early and reached the Hidden Beach before any other boat. Half an hour of snorkeling with nobody around.
reviews.author: Sofía and Emilio

reviews.quote: Whales on the way out and blue-footed boobies on the way back. Twelve people on the boat makes a difference.
reviews.author: Javier M.

avistamiento-de-ballenas.name: Whale watching
avistamiento-de-ballenas.headline: Whale watching
avistamiento-de-ballenas.short: Season from December to March. A short trip with a certified guide and guaranteed sighting windows.
avistamiento-de-ballenas.pitch: From December to March, four hours with a certified guide and a hydrophone on board.
avistamiento-de-ballenas.blurb: Every winter the humpbacks come to Banderas Bay to give birth and raise their calves. We sail for four hours with a certified guide and a hydrophone on board to hear them sing. If we do not see them, you repeat the trip at no cost.
avistamiento-de-ballenas.photoAlt: Humpback whale breaching in Banderas Bay

itinerary.title: Nuevo Vallarta dock
itinerary.body: Check-in, life jacket and coffee. The captain explains the day's route from the sea report.

itinerary.title: We sail
itinerary.body: Forty minutes towards open sea. On the way we often cross paths with dolphins and rays.

itinerary.title: Sighting area
itinerary.body: Two hours off Punta Mita with the engine off. We lower the hydrophone to hear the song.

itinerary.title: Back along the bay
itinerary.body: We return hugging the coast. Arrival at the dock around 12:00.

includes: You repeat if we do not see them

faq.question: What if we do not see whales?
faq.answer: You repeat the trip at no cost on any day you like within the season. In ten years it has happened to us four times.

faq.question: Which departure is better, morning or afternoon?
faq.answer: The 8:00 am one has the flattest sea; the 3:00 pm one comes back with the sunset light. Whale activity is similar in both.

faq.question: Can children come?
faq.answer: Yes. We carry life jackets in every size and the trip is short. For children under 4 we recommend the private boat.

faq.question: How close does the boat get?
faq.answer: Mexican regulations require 60 meters of distance and engines off. If they come closer on their own, we stay still.

reviews.quote: We left in the afternoon and came back with the sunset. The guide explained everything without turning it into a lecture.
reviews.author: Iván P.

reviews.quote: A mother with her calf thirty meters from the boat. Nobody spoke, only the hydrophone.
reviews.author: Sofía M.

reviews.quote: The first day they did not show up and we were allowed to repeat at no cost. The second day we saw four.
reviews.author: Karla and Beto

charter-privado.name: Private charter
charter-privado.headline: Private charter
charter-privado.short: The whole boat for your group: route, schedule and menu your way. Weddings, birthdays and company outings.
charter-privado.pitch: The whole boat for your group: route, schedule and menu your way.
charter-privado.blurb: The whole boat, the route you want and the schedule that suits you. We bring the crew, the music, the bar and the food; you decide where to anchor, how long to stay and when to head back.
charter-privado.photoAlt: Private boat sailing across the bay
charter-privado.itineraryTitle: A typical day, to give you an idea

itinerary.title: The dock, at your time
itinerary.body: Departures from 8:00 am. The boat is waiting with the music and the bar ready.

itinerary.title: First stop
itinerary.body: Snorkeling at Los Arcos or Las Caletas, depending on the route we have put together.

itinerary.title: Lunch on board
itinerary.body: A menu your way: ceviche, grilled fish or whatever the group orders ahead of time.

itinerary.title: Beach and sunset
itinerary.body: We anchor at Las Ánimas or Majahuitas for kayaking, paddle boarding and a swim to the shore.

itinerary.title: Return
itinerary.body: Back to the dock with the sunset or, if the group prefers, at night with the lights of the boardwalk.

faq.question: How many people fit on the boat?
faq.answer: Up to 16 people comfortably. For bigger groups we sail with two boats side by side.

faq.question: How is it priced?
faq.answer: By sailing hours and number of people. Tell us the date, the group and the idea of the route and we quote on WhatsApp the same day.

faq.question: Can we bring our own food and drinks?
faq.answer: Yes, at no charge. If you prefer, we put the menu and the bar together for you in advance.

faq.question: Do you do weddings and events?
faq.answer: Yes. Weddings, birthdays, bachelor parties and company outings. We can arrange decoration, cake and a photographer with local suppliers.

terms.title: Terms and conditions
terms.lead: The rules we run every trip by: what a booking covers, what happens when the weather turns and what we expect from everyone on board.

sections.heading: Who runs the trips
sections.body: Vallarta WKND runs boat trips inside Bahía de Banderas with local captains and crew. Booking any of our experiences means you accept these terms; if any of them does not work for you, write to us before you confirm.

sections.heading: Bookings and deposit
sections.body: A booking is confirmed once we receive the 30% deposit; the rest is paid on the day of the trip, before we cast off. Seats are held in the order they are confirmed, not in the order they are asked for.

sections.heading: Changes and cancellations
sections.body: You can move or cancel your trip free of charge up to 48 hours before departure and we return the full deposit. Inside those 48 hours the deposit stays with us as credit, good for six months on the date you choose.

sections.heading: Weather and sea conditions
sections.body: Safety comes first: the captain may delay, shorten, reroute or cancel a trip because of wind, swell or a port authority notice. When the cancellation is ours, you choose between moving the date and getting everything you paid back.

sections.heading: Timing and boarding
sections.body: Please arrive 30 minutes before departure at the dock named in your confirmation. The boat cannot wait for latecomers, and in that case the trip counts as taken.

sections.heading: Safety on board
sections.body: Life jackets are compulsory while under way and the captain's instructions are followed at all times. We may refuse boarding, or end a trip, if someone puts the group at risk or arrives in no condition to sail.

sections.heading: Minors, health and responsibility
sections.body: Minors always travel with a responsible adult. If you are pregnant, have reduced mobility or a condition that gets worse at sea, tell us when you book: some activities, snorkeling among them, may not be for you.

sections.heading: Prices and payment
sections.body: Prices are published in Mexican pesos per person and include what each experience lists. We may update them at any time, but they never change the price of a booking that is already confirmed.

sections.heading: Photographs and content
sections.body: The copy, photographs and marks on this site are ours or used with permission. If we take pictures on board and want to publish them, we ask you first; saying no changes nothing about your trip.

sections.heading: Applicable law
sections.body: These terms are governed by the laws of Mexico, and anything that needs sorting out is handled first between us, in Puerto Vallarta, Jalisco, or before PROFECO where that applies.

privacy.title: Privacy notice
privacy.lead: What we ask for in order to take you out to sea, what we use it for and how you ask us to delete it.

sections.heading: Who is responsible for your data
sections.body: Vallarta WKND, based in Puerto Vallarta, Jalisco, is responsible for the personal data you share with us through this site, over WhatsApp or by phone.

sections.heading: What we collect
sections.body: Only what a trip needs: name, phone number, email address, date, departure time and number of people. If you tell us something about your health that matters for the activity, we keep it only until the trip is over.

sections.heading: What we use it for
sections.body: To confirm your booking, arrange boarding, warn you about weather changes, issue your receipt and answer your questions before and after the trip.

sections.heading: Additional purposes
sections.body: If you let us, we write now and then about seasons and offers. You can ask us to stop at any time and you will still be able to book exactly as before.

sections.heading: Who we share it with
sections.body: With the captain and crew of your trip, and with the payment processor when you pay by card. We do not sell or trade your data with third parties for advertising.

sections.heading: Your data rights
sections.body: You can access, correct or delete your data, or object to its use, by writing to our contact address. We answer within 20 working days and ask nothing in return.

sections.heading: Cookies and analytics
sections.body: The site uses no advertising or profiling cookies. We store only the minimum in your browser, so it remembers the language you are reading in.

sections.heading: How long we keep it
sections.body: Booking data is kept for as long as tax and accounting rules require; everything else is deleted once there is no reason to hold on to it.

sections.heading: Changes to this notice
sections.body: When something important changes we publish it here and update the date at the top. The version on this page is always the one in force.
